newsitem.title: UK: European gasoline pours into U.S. in Sept - trade.
newsitem.headline: European gasoline pours into U.S. in Sept - trade.

text.p: Europe's gasoline market has tightened considerably following the sale of at least 270,000 tonnes of September-loading gasoline to transatlantic destinations, traders and brokers said.

Shipping brokers said two 60,000-tonne cargoes had been fixed to move to the U.S. Atlantic Coast, in addition to 150,000 tonnes reported by Reuters last week sold to various transatlantic destinations.
The arbitrage window was marginally open again on Wednesday, dealers said, after Iraq-related gyrations in futures prices closed it on Tuesday.
But they said it would be hard to sell much more out of Europe because there are few barrels left in the region.
Shipping brokers said traders Vitol had fixed both of the latest clean tankers -- a 63,000 tonner loading in the U.K. on Thursday and 62,000 tonnes from northern Spain at the end of the month.
A European broker said the first ship, the Ariel, contained 30,000 tonnes of gasoline originating in Milford Haven, and 30,000 tonnes from another U.K. refinery.
Traders said the second tanker, the Bow Transporter, contained reformulated gasoline from Petronor's Bilbao refinery.
Vitol was not available for comment.

In addition to these two cargoes, Reuters reported last week that 60,000 tonnes of 87 and 93 octane gasoline was sold transatlantic out of Killingholme last week, and European brokers said that was due to load on Friday.

Another 28,000 tonne cargo, loading this week, was sold to a transatlantic destination out of France, as well as a third cargo containing 60,000 tonnes of gasoline sourced out of Antwerp, which brokers said would load this week too.
